excerpt: Grok 4.6, SpaceXAI's frontier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, is now available on the xAI API. It has a 500k context window
Expose any internal API, database, or SaaS tool to Grok. Define your own tools with custom schemas and logic.
A tunneling service solves this by exposing your local server through a public URL that Grok can connect to.
Speech to Text now accepts a vad_threshold parameter (streaming query param and batch multipart field) to tune the voice-activity gate
You can now request higher scheduling priority per request by setting service_tier: "priority" on text inference endpoints
Requests to the slug will be served by grok-imagine-image-2.0 with quality set to low, with no change to the request or response shape
Create images and video with Grok Imagine.
Image editing now accepts up to 5 source images per request (was 3).
New aspect ratios. Image generation and editing accept 21:9 (cinematic widescreen) and 5:2 (wide banners).
grok-imagine-video-1.5 now supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and reference-to-video (including optional preset voices), with native 1080p for T2V and I2V.
Connect your tools so Grok can reach your email, files, and calendar right inside a chat.
Paid SuperGrok plans raise your limits and unlock more across every product, drawing from a single weekly usage allowance you can spend however you like.
In your team workspace, enjoy enterprise-grade privacy protections... Additionally, unlock the full capabilities of SuperGrok, including higher usage quotas and advanced features.
Share conversations only with team members who have active licenses.
Grok Bot — hand real work to AI teammates on a persistent cloud computer.
Create new records - Add Leads, Opportunities, Accounts, Cases, or records on custom objects directly from chat.
Secure and streamline logins by integrating Single Sign-On (SSO) with your preferred Identity Provider (IdP).
Invite new team members to join your Grok Business workspace with a simple email invitation process.
Built-in connectors are maintained by xAI and integrate natively with Grok. Each one authenticates via OAuth, so you connect once and Grok can access your data on demand.
Generate text, have conversations, use tools, and build AI-powered applications.
previous input prompts, reasoning content, and model responses are saved and stored on xAI's servers
Streaming outputs is **supported by all models with text output capability**
grok-4.6` and `grok-4.5` support the `reasoning_effort` parameter, which controls how much effort the model spends thinking before responding.
Structured Outputs lets the API return responses in a specific format, for example, a JSON object matching a schema you define
Some models allow images in the input. The model will consider the image context when generating the response.
Realtime Multi-agent Research enables Grok to orchestrate multiple AI agents that work together in real time to perform deep, multi-step research tasks.
Send a coding prompt to Grok Build (`grok-4.6`) and get a response.
Generate images from text prompts with Grok Imagine models. The API supports batch generation of multiple images, and control over aspect ratio, resolution, and quality.
Edit an existing image by providing a source image along with your prompt. The model understands the image content and applies your requested changes.
Use up to five source images for a single image edit.
Generate videos from text prompts with Grok video models. The API supports configurable duration, aspect ratio, and resolution
Transform a still image into a video by providing a source image along with an optional prompt.
Provide reference images, a preset voice, or both to guide the generated video.
`grok-imagine-video` delivers high-fidelity edits with strong scene preservation, modifying only what you ask for while keeping the rest of the video intact
Search emails using Gmail search operators (`from:`, `to:`, `subject:`, `newer_than:`, `has:attachment`, etc.).
The Google Drive connector lets Grok search, read, and manage files in your Google Drive.
Search across channels and chats, read messages, send new messages, reply to threads, and create chats — all without leaving Grok.
When you add a custom MCP connector, Grok's servers need to reach your MCP server over the public internet.
Switch between workspaces to access team-specific features and ensure your conversations are protected under business plan terms.
Talk to Grok hands-free with voice.
Sign in once and your conversations, settings, and subscription stay in sync across every platform.
Visit grok.com/?_s=billing while logged in to manage your billing directly from the website (change plan, update payment, or cancel).

Of the 3 models I tried, Grok did the best at making an iOS app I wanted for personal use... Grok definitely fumbles sometimes, but I have been surprised what it CAN intuit versus me having to micromanage it.

Very fast, easily beats GPT 5.5/Opus 4.8/GLM 5.2 because of higher t/s (around 90?) and very high token efficiency. Very good price... I'd say in the same tier as opus, occupying the lower end of that tier together with GLM 5.2.
Tried this for a legal use case and it was excellent, comparable to Opus in quality but much faster... the output was similar to a law student intern. But coherent and directionally correct.
They talk about benchmark first places at every release, but in reality from 4.0 onward Grok got worse every release. So bad in fact that they removed the login-free access and rented out colossus.
Every time I get excited about Grok's performance on benchmarks and demo videos, I test it myself and end up disappointed.

I experimented with Grok 4 for openclaw... It was more verbally fluid than 5.5, but had real trouble with agentic tool calling - the model felt like it hadn't been trained to think of tool calling as one of its primary modalities.
still waiting for a proper gui for grok build - terminal is nice but codex desktop app is very useful
Asked a one-word opinion question, Grok appears to search X for posts 'from:elonmusk' on topics like Israel/Palestine before answering, seemingly defaulting to Musk's views as the tiebreaker.
I've seen reports that if you ask Grok (v3) about links between Musk and Jeffrey Epstein it switches to the first person and answers as if it was Elon himself in the response.
Elon likes to meddle with Grok whenever the mood strikes him, leading to Grok's sudden interest in Nazi topics such as South African 'white genocide' and calling itself MechaHitler.
Karpathy gave his initial impression: the impression overall I got here is that this is somewhere around (OpenAI) o1-pro capability.
Grok has gotten to the top of one benchmark (lmarena) - Grok 3 at the top of Chatbot Arena with 1400, and the model will continue to improve as it trains more.

I am excited for the voice mode promised in 'a week' or so. ChatGPT Advanced Voice has been a big disappointment for me... If Grok 3 voice mode can discuss current events from the X timeline then it should be much more interesting to talk to.
grok.com returned: 500 Internal Server Error, nginx/1.27.4 shortly after launch.

I think they put the new model behind a $40 paywall so less people use it. The model seems only marginally better than open source models, based on xAI's own internal tests, and they spend $$$ for it to run.
Musk already has too much power, won't trust him with my AI conversations.
